project.title: Monthly performance against benchmark for the family council
project.subtitle: One new project run end to end in Signal Harbor: from Mei Chen's own words to a live pipeline, an approved dashboard and delivery, with every screen captured as it happened.
project.footnote: Evergreen Office is a synthetic family office. All data, documents and people are synthetic. Testing mode (low-cost models) on a private test environment, 11 Oct 2026.
project.paragraph: Every month the family council wants one page showing how the liquid portfolio EG-LIQUID did against the family benchmark EG-OFFICE-BLEND: portfolio return, benchmark return and the difference in points, ready by the 5th business day so the council can decide whether to rebalance. Today Mei Chen builds it by hand in Excel over two days. In this walkthrough Mei described the need to North. Daniel Foo signed the intent and Mei handed it to Leo Park. Span the architect drafted the design pack and Anita Rao approved it. Span the builder ran it on a copy and checked it against September's issued report (4.17%, 2.71%, 1.46 points): every line matched. A corrected pack version 2 was approved and rerun, and the pipeline went live. Lumen proposed a starter dashboard; Daniel approved it and it was set up for Consume and a monthly council email. Two things did not work: Mei's own tile (the difference) could not be added, and the approved dashboard does not appear in Consume. The fifteen findings at the end say what to fix.

steps.who: Mei Chen (business owner)

steps.happened: The landing shows the four steps (Intent with North, Architecture with Span, Pipelines with Span, Dashboards and delivery with Lumen), the chapters film and the one project already running (Monthly investment report in USD and SGD, live).
steps.if_wrong: Company admin (Grace Ong) checks Mei's access to Build.

steps.who: Mei Chen (business owner)
steps.intended: Start a new project from Build.
steps.did: Clicked New project.
steps.happened: A new project opens on the Intent step with North; Mei is asked to say what she needs in her own words.
steps.if_wrong: Company admin (Grace Ong) if the button is missing for Mei's role.

steps.who: Mei Chen (business owner), with North (agent)
steps.intended: Mei says in her own words what she needs, which sources feed it and how each arrives; North drafts the intent of work and the process map as they talk.
steps.did: Ten messages by Mei: the need (EG-LIQUID against EG-OFFICE-BLEND, 5th business day), readers and decision, the four sources with how they arrive (Excel export, index CSV, manager PDFs, last month's report, all by upload), the figures and September's reported values (4.17 / 2.71 / 1.46), today's five steps, access, retention and success; then the result layout, the version 2 open point (Raj Patel) and a request to mark the intent ready. Each North proposal was accepted; the process map was confirmed with That's right.
steps.happened: North asked one question per turn and drafted as it went, e.g. 'Got the September 2026 figures - portfolio return 4.17 %, benchmark return 2.71 %, difference 1.46 points - and noted they should read the same after the load.' It once said 'We still need the version 2 benchmark weights before the pack can be signed'; Mei answered that version 2 is an open point for Raj Patel. After Mei asked, North wrote its closing summary and 'Sign the intent of work' appeared. Gaps: the summary lists each figure as 'no source yet' although Mei named the sources, keeps 'Who should be allowed to see this work?' as unclear although Mei named the four people, and the goal line is cut mid-word ('so the council can de').
steps.if_wrong: Mei corrects any section with North (or the edit link); a wrong figure definition goes to Raj Patel (finance) before signing.

steps.who: Daniel Foo (sponsor)
steps.intended: The sponsor reads the intent of work and signs it, so the data team may start.
steps.did: Daniel opened Action, found the card 'Intent to sign', opened the sign page, ticked that he had read every section and pressed Sign intent.
steps.happened: Action showed the intent to sign. The intent is signed and read-only; Build opens on the project. The signed definition of 'Return difference' reads 'difference in basis points ... (benchmark - portfolio)': North reversed the sign and changed the unit from what Mei said, and the sign page did not flag it.
steps.if_wrong: Mei Chen reopens the intent with North and fixes the section Daniel queries; Daniel signs again.

steps.step: Hand over to the data engineer

steps.if_wrong: Anita Rao (head of data) reassigns the work to another data engineer.

steps.step: Architecture: what I already know, confirm the systems
steps.who: Leo Park (data engineer), with Span the architect (agent)
steps.intended: Span reads the signed intent and shows each source as the intent recorded it; Leo confirms rather than re-entering.
steps.did: Leo opened the project's Architecture step and pressed Confirm on each of the four sources.
steps.happened: Span: 'I read the signed intent and the process map (5 steps). I scanned what already arrives. I only need to ask you 6 things.' The four sources (administrator positions export, index levels, manager statements, last month's report) carry 'from the intent' with how and when they arrive (upload, monthly); the three signed figures are listed. All four confirmed; status 'Never seen', nothing landed yet. Last month's report is listed as a source like the others, not as the benchmark to check against.
steps.if_wrong: Leo presses 'This is different' and corrects the channel; the intent's system map and the pack change together. Mei answers if the source itself is wrong.

steps.who: Leo Park (data engineer), with Span the architect (agent)
steps.intended: Span asks only what the intent and the scan cannot answer, each with a proposed default; Leo accepts or edits.
steps.did: Span asked four questions (grain, history, checks, freshness). Leo wanted the grain 'monthly by portfolio' instead of Span's 'monthly by entity'; the screen offers only Accept for grain, so he pressed Accept all and continue (history: none beyond values by date; checks: loaded total equals the source footer; freshness: 06:00 monthly, by the 5th business day), then re-answered the grain as 'monthly by portfolio' outside the screen, because the screen has no way to edit it (typing it as plain text was refused: 'That answer does not fit the question.').
steps.happened: All four answered, grain now by portfolio. Span did not ask again for sources, definitions or access, which the intent already held. The two PDF sources remain open as 'mark the fields' sample questions.
steps.if_wrong: Leo re-answers a question; Anita Rao (head of data) settles a disputed grain or check at pack approval.
steps.outcome: Done, one answer changed outside the screen

steps.step: Architecture: samples (upload the Excel, mark the PDF fields)
steps.who: Leo Park (data engineer), with Span the architect (agent)
steps.intended: Show Span one file of each never-seen source and mark, once, the fields to read on the PDFs.
steps.did: Leo chose the files on the Samples tab: the Harbourline positions export (.xlsx) and the index levels (.csv); then the Evergreen Growth I statement (PDF) and marked fund_name, statement_date and net_asset_value on their lines; then last month's report (PDF) and marked portfolio_return, benchmark_return and difference.
steps.happened: Span profiled both tables and proposed where each column goes (e.g. Market Value to position_snapshots.source_market_value, date to market_observations.observed_at); 'to confirm' on Admin Code, Price, Valuation Status, Valuation Date and on both index columns. The statement shows 'Net asset value: 10,180,000' and the marks are listed: 'Span will read these from every statement.' The first PDFs, laid out as two-column tables, could not be marked (each cell became its own line); they were re-issued with one 'label: value' line each.
steps.if_wrong: Leo re-marks a field; if the statement layout changes, Mei asks the manager for the standard statement; Anita reviews the mapping at approval.

steps.step: Architecture: the design pack and the mapping sheet
steps.who: Leo Park (data engineer), with Span the architect (agent)
steps.intended: Span drafts one versioned design pack (target model, catalogue, mapping sheet, rules, sources, benchmark check); Leo settles what needs a person and sends it to the head of data.
steps.did: Leo pressed Draft the design pack, read the Target model, Catalogue, ETL mapping sheet, Rules and Sources tabs, settled the two open mapping rows with a note each, and pressed Send to the head of data for approval.
steps.happened: Pack version 1: 4 sources, 2 gold and 5 silver tables, 19 mapping rows (2 open), 1 check. Gold: returns by portfolio and month (portfolio_return, benchmark_return, difference as DECIMAL(9,6)) and the weight of each benchmark leg; benchmark block EG-LIQUID against EG-OFFICE-BLEND version 1 for 2026-09. The marked PDF fields map to 'Read the value after Net asset value on every statement'. The two open rows were the Excel and CSV samples ('Sample kept; map it before it feeds a table'): the gold returns are computed from the company model (position snapshots, market observations, benchmark components), not from the uploaded files, so Leo settled them in words. Gold table names are cut mid-word ('gold_monthly_performance_against_be_...'). Status: waiting for the head of data.
steps.if_wrong: Leo corrects a line (a new version); Span redrafts from the latest answers; Anita Rao rejects with a note if the model is wrong.

steps.step: Anita approves the design pack (and the build plan)
steps.who: Anita Rao (head of data), Leo Park (data engineer)
steps.intended: The head of data approves the pack; approved means locked for the builder.
steps.did: Anita opened Action ('Design pack v1: Monthly performance against benchmark', from Leo Park), reviewed the pack and pressed Approve version 1. Leo pressed Draw the build plan from this pack. Anita then approved the plan drawn from it ('the builder may try it on a copy').
steps.happened: 'Approved by Anita Rao. Locked for the builder; the team can still edit it through a new version.' Plan version 1 drawn from pack version 1 and approved; plan state 'built'. The product asks the head of data to approve twice (the pack, then the plan drawn from it), where the agreed flow has one approval. (The screens for drawing the plan and for approving it repeated earlier captures, so one plan screen is shown.)
steps.if_wrong: Anita rejects with a note; Leo corrects the pack and resubmits. The maker cannot approve their own version.

steps.step: Pipelines: connect and run on a copy (automatic)
steps.who: Leo Park (data engineer), with Span the builder (agent)
steps.intended: The builder connects each source exactly as the pack says (uploads this month) and runs the pipeline on a copy without waiting for a click.
steps.did: Leo opened Pipelines. Nothing was clicked: the builder had already started when the plan was approved.
steps.happened: Span the builder: 'I took design pack version 1 as it was approved. I connect each source as it says and run on a copy. I only come back to you when something fails.' 4 of 4 connected (the positions export and index CSV that landed as samples; the marked fields 'from each statement (104 on file for the company)'). Run on a copy: Done, started by itself at 22:18. 6 tables built (4 bronze, 0 silver, 2 gold), 60 gold rows, checks 0 of 1 (control totals against the source files). The bronze tables say 'no mapping is approved yet'. The three other manager statements were not landed: Pipelines has no upload for this month's files, the Architecture sample takes one PDF per source, and the company intake page takes only Excel or CSV.
steps.if_wrong: The builder comes back to Leo when a connection fails; Mei provides a missing file; Anita decides if a source must change (a new pack version).

steps.who: Leo Park (data engineer), with Span the builder (agent)
steps.intended: The builder asks for last month's report, reads it and compares every figure it can find with the run, line by line.
steps.did: Span asked: 'Do you have last month's report to check against? I will compare every figure I can find in it.' Leo uploaded the September report as issued (PDF).
steps.happened: 'Check against monthly_performance_report_2026-09.pdf: Variance cleared.' Portfolio return 4.17% against 4.17% (run 4.1667), Office blend 2.71% against 2.71% (run 2.7072), Difference 1.46% against 1.46% (run 1.4595), all Matches; legs: global equity 42%, global bond 28%, private-markets sleeve 30%, all Matches. 'Looks good. Going live uses the schedule in the pack: every month at 06:00.' There was no variance, so 'Send back to the architect' was not offered.
steps.if_wrong: On an unexplained line Leo sends it back to Span the architect with the evidence; the architect issues the next pack version for Anita Rao to approve; the builder reruns by itself.

steps.step: Pack version 2: Leo corrects the definitions
steps.who: Leo Park (data engineer), as Span the architect's reviewer
steps.intended: With no variance to send back, Leo reads the approved pack once more before going live and corrects what is wrong through a new version.
steps.did: In the gold columns, Leo pressed Correct a line on four definitions: portfolio_code and benchmark_code (both tables) carried the text of a return KPI ('Time-weighted monthly return of the EG-LIQUID portfolio, net of fees'), and the difference column did not say its unit or that the signed intent text disagrees. He opened Compare versions (1 to 2) and sent version 2 to the head of data.
steps.happened: Correcting an approved pack forked version 2 as a draft (version 1 stays locked). Compare versions lists the four changes, old text struck through. Version 2: waiting for the head of data. The 'Send back to the architect' path was not exercised in this walk because the first run matched the report.
steps.if_wrong: Anita Rao rejects version 2 with a note; version 1 stays the approved one.

steps.step: Approve pack version 2; the builder reruns by itself
steps.who: Anita Rao (head of data), Leo Park (data engineer), with Span the builder (agent)
steps.intended: The head of data approves the new version; the builder reruns on a copy without being asked and checks the report again.
steps.did: Anita pressed Approve version 2; Leo drew plan version 2 from it; Anita approved the plan ('Plan version 2 from pack version 2 (definitions only)'). Leo reopened Pipelines.
steps.happened: Pack version 2 approved and locked. The builder ran pack version 2 on a copy by itself and checked it against the same report: 'Variance cleared', Pack version 2, the three figures and three legs all Matches.
steps.if_wrong: If the rerun fails or a line no longer matches, the builder holds it and Leo sends it back to the architect; Anita approves the fix.

steps.who: Leo Park (data engineer), with Span the builder (agent)
steps.intended: With the check clean, take the pipeline live on the pack's schedule.
steps.did: Leo pressed Go live on the Pipelines step.
steps.happened: The round is live: 'Live on the pack schedule, every month at 06:00. Lumen proposes a starter dashboard.' The builder hands on to Lumen for a starter dashboard.
steps.if_wrong: Leo or Anita Rao stops the schedule; a failed scheduled run comes back to Leo in Action.

steps.who: Mei Chen (business owner), with Lumen (agent)
steps.intended: When the pipeline goes live, Lumen proposes a starter dashboard from the intent's figures, readers and breakdowns, so nothing is built from scratch.
steps.did: Mei opened the Dashboards step: 'Lumen's starter dashboard, Draft, version 1, 6 widgets, made by Lumen', and opened it in the studio.
steps.happened: Lumen: 'The pipeline is live. I put this together from the signed intent so nothing has to be built from scratch... It reads gold, pack version 2.' Tiles: Portfolio return in the latest month, EG-LIQUID only, 4.17% (twice, the same tile); a monthly trend of liquid portfolio return against benchmark return (axis in fractions, -0.02 to 0.04); portfolio return by portfolio code (all four portfolios, bars down to about -50%); portfolio return by benchmark code (one bar near -90%); a checks status line ('2 of 6 steps ok'). No benchmark return or difference figure tile, although the intent names both. The refresh line reads 'day 5 of each month at 06:00; next 5 Nov 2026'.
steps.if_wrong: Mei removes or asks Lumen to change a tile; Leo checks a figure that does not match gold ('Where is this from?').

steps.who: Mei Chen (business owner), with Lumen (agent)
steps.intended: Mei asks Lumen for one specific addition, the difference in percentage points for the latest month, and accepts it onto the starter.
steps.did: Mei asked Lumen in the studio's Talk to Lumen: 'Add one figure tile: the difference between the EG-LIQUID portfolio return and the EG-OFFICE-BLEND benchmark return in the latest month, in percentage points.' (twice, once with the starter opened by its own link). Then she used the widget library (empty slot, Figure, table '...benchmark monthly', Add widget to the slot). Then she tried to select that tile and ask Lumen to turn it into the difference.
steps.happened: Lumen replied 'I have proposed one tile, Difference at the latest date, EG-LIQUID and EG-OFFICE-BLEND only. It is waiting for you: accept it or choose Not this.', but no Accept button appeared: each ask placed the proposal on a new, empty personal 'My dashboard' (three were made), not on the starter the studio shows. The widget library added a figure 'Portfolio return' (the first column), not the difference, and offers no column choice. Selecting the tile did not register, and Lumen's next reply went off topic ('...I am holding off on the chart request to focus solely on the approval workflow'). The requested difference tile was NOT added; the starter carries one extra 'Portfolio return' figure.
steps.if_wrong: Leo Park adds the tile in the studio from the gold column; the Lumen defect goes to the product team.

steps.who: Mei Chen, then Daniel Foo (sponsor)
steps.intended: Mei sends the dashboard for approval; someone other than its maker approves it.
steps.did: Mei pressed Send for approval on the starter. Daniel opened Action, then the dashboard, read 'What Lumen checked' and pressed Approve.
steps.happened: Daniel's Action showed 'Dashboard: Lumen's starter dashboard, from Mei Chen'. 'What Lumen checked': tiles name their source (checked); readers are the project's people (checked); but 'The month's numbers - not checked: No reviewed run is on record for this project' and 'The benchmark is the signed definition - not checked: No signed benchmark version is on record', although the builder's check matched the report and EG-OFFICE-BLEND version 1 is signed. Daniel approved; the dashboard is published.
steps.if_wrong: Daniel sends it back with a reason; Mei changes the tiles and sends it again.

steps.step: Delivery: Consume and the council email
steps.who: Mei Chen (business owner), Daniel Foo (sponsor)
steps.intended: Mei chooses where the approved dashboard goes (Consume and a monthly email digest to the council); someone else approves each channel; then delivery goes live.
steps.did: Mei added Consume and an Email digest (monthly, 07:00, to family.council@evergreen-office.example.test, a synthetic address), opened the email Preview and sent both for approval; Daniel approved both; Mei pressed Go live.
steps.happened: Both channels approved and live. The email preview (subject 'Lumen's starter dashboard: portfolio return 0.0417') lists each tile in words, e.g. 'Portfolio return in the latest month, EG-LIQUID only: portfolio return 0.0417' and 'Portfolio return by benchmark code in the latest month: benchmark code EG-OFFICE-BLEND, portfolio return -0.8715'. Figures are raw fractions, not percentages, and the implausible bar values travel into the email. The outbox is empty: 'Nothing is sent when you press Go live'; the first message goes at the next scheduled time, so no sent email could be shown. The first attempt left the email channel in draft (only Consume was submitted); it was submitted and approved on a second pass.
steps.if_wrong: Daniel sends a channel back with a reason, or Mei stops it; a failed send stays in the outbox with Send again.

steps.who: Mei Chen (business owner)
steps.intended: The project's complete page records who signed, approved and delivered what, and adds the work to the company knowledge map.
steps.did: Mei opened the project's complete page.
steps.happened: 'PROJECT COMPLETE - 11 OCT 2026. Monthly performance against benchmark is live. Lumen now runs it; you only hear from it when something needs you.' Intent signed by Daniel Foo; architecture approved by Anita Rao; pipelines 'Live, started by Leo Park after a clean check'; dashboards 'Approved and delivered to 2 channels'. Added to the company knowledge map: 10 items (4 sources, 2 gold tables, the dashboard, Mei as owner, Daniel as sponsor, Leo as builder), each verified only where a record says so.

steps.step: Consume and the Map show the result
steps.who: Daniel Foo (sponsor), Anita Rao (head of data)
steps.intended: Daniel reads the result in Consume; Anita sees the project, its sources and tables on the company map.
steps.did: Daniel opened Consume, its Dashboards list and Shared with you. Anita opened the Map and the project on it.
steps.happened: Consume's Morning Note reads 'The Evergreen Liquid portfolio returned 4.17% in September, 1.46 points ahead of its benchmark' with a Certified tile 'Liquid book, September 4.17%, Benchmark 2.71% +1.46 pts' (the same figures the pipeline matched). But the new dashboard is not listed under Consume > Dashboards or Shared with you, for Daniel or Mei, although its Consume channel is approved and live; only the earlier project's dashboard shows. The Map lists 'Monthly performance against benchmark - Live' beside the earlier project, with its sources (Administrator positions export, Global equity and bond index levels, Last month's report, Manager statements); 19 items from finished projects wait for the head of data before they join the verified map.
steps.if_wrong: Mei checks the Consume channel on the delivery page; Anita reviews the 19 waiting map items.
steps.outcome: Not as intended: dashboard missing from Consume

summary.elapsed_text: In the product, from Mei's first sentence to North (21:46 Singapore time) to delivery live (about 22:31): about 45 minutes, of which about 10 minutes were the conversation with North. The time recorded inside the 21 steps adds up to about 25 minutes; the rest was handing over between people. Each person acted only at their own points; the agents drafted, ran and checked in between. The whole walkthrough took about 63 minutes of wall-clock time: rebuilding the product screens, seeding the environment, making the sources and diagnosing the defects listed below.
agents: North: 13 model calls; asked one question per turn, drafted the intent sections, the three figure definitions and the 5-step process map, wrote the closing summary

Span the architect: read the signed intent (never asked again for sources, channels or definitions), asked 4 questions with defaults, profiled two samples, drafted the design pack (2 gold, 5 silver tables, 19 mapping rows, benchmark block), versioned the correction and showed the comparison

Span the builder: connected 4 sources, ran on a copy by itself at approval (6 tables, 60 gold rows), read the uploaded report and compared 6 lines (all matched), reran pack version 2 by itself and rechecked
Lumen: proposed a starter dashboard with 6 widgets from the signed intent; listed what it checked for the approver; wrote the delivery previews
people: Mei Chen: 10 messages to North; hand-over; asked for one tile; sent the dashboard for approval; set up two delivery channels and pressed Go live
Daniel Foo: signed the intent; approved the dashboard and both channels
Anita Rao: approved pack version 1, its plan, pack version 2 and its plan
Leo Park: confirmed 4 sources, answered 4 questions, gave 4 samples and marked 6 fields, settled 2 mapping rows, corrected 4 definitions, uploaded the benchmark report, pressed Go live
summary.cost_text: Testing mode throughout (Real use never switched on). 26 model calls, about 198,000 tokens, 0.0106 USD in total from the product's cost log (North 13 calls, 0.0066 USD; the rest Lumen and summaries). Budget was under 1 USD.

findings.title: Mei's specific tile could not be added
findings.text: Asking Lumen for a tile while the starter is open puts the proposal on a new hidden personal 'My dashboard' (three were made), so Lumen says it waits for Accept but no Accept appears. The widget library's Figure takes the first column (portfolio return) with no column choice; selecting a tile to change it did not register; a later Lumen reply went off topic. The difference tile was not added.

findings.title: The delivered dashboard is missing from Consume
findings.text: Approved and delivered to a live Consume channel, yet not listed under Consume > Dashboards or Shared with you for Daniel or Mei. Consume shows the same figures only through the seeded Morning Note.

findings.title: North reversed a signed definition
findings.text: The 'Return difference' figure was drafted as 'difference in basis points (benchmark - portfolio)'; Mei said portfolio minus benchmark in percentage points. The sign page did not flag it and Daniel signed it. The pack computes portfolio minus benchmark, so the signed text and the build disagree (noted in pack version 2).

findings.title: Lumen's starter tiles are partly wrong
findings.text: The same 4.17% tile twice; no tile for the benchmark return or the difference although the intent names both; by-portfolio and by-benchmark-code bars at about -50% and -90% (probably values added up across months or portfolios); trend axis in fractions next to tiles in percent; white number boxes on the dark theme. The email preview carries the same raw fractions (0.0417, -0.8715).

findings.title: Approval panel says the numbers were not checked
findings.text: 'What Lumen checked' shows 'No reviewed run is on record' and 'No signed benchmark version is on record' after the builder's check matched the report and with EG-OFFICE-BLEND version 1 signed.

findings.title: The gold tables do not read this month's files
findings.text: The pack's gold tables read the company model (positions, market observations, benchmark legs), not the uploaded Excel and CSV: both stayed 'Sample kept; map it before it feeds a table' and were settled in words. Bronze says 'no mapping is approved yet'; checks 0 of 1 after the run. The cycle proves the calculation on data already in the warehouse, not the ingestion of these files.

findings.title: No place to land this month's further PDFs
findings.text: Pipelines has no upload; the Architecture sample takes one PDF per source; the intake page takes only Excel or CSV. The three other manager statements were not landed. The statement count reads '104 on file for the company', not this project.

findings.title: PDF tables cannot be read
findings.text: The PDF reader puts each table cell on its own line, so a statement or report laid out as a two-column table cannot be marked. The walkthrough's first PDFs used tables and were re-issued with one 'label: value' line each.

findings.title: North needed prompting to finish
findings.text: With every required section filled North did not mark the intent ready; it asked for the version 2 weights (not needed) and wrote the closing summary only when Mei asked. The summary listed each figure as 'no source yet', kept 'who may see this' as unclear after Mei named four people, and cut the goal mid-word ('so the council can de').

findings.title: Grain cannot be edited on screen
findings.text: The few questions offers only Accept for grain (Span proposed 'monthly by entity' for a per-portfolio figure); the change had to be entered outside the screen.

findings.title: Pack version 1 had copied definitions
findings.text: portfolio_code and benchmark_code carried a return KPI's definition text; the Definitions panel lists 2 of the 3 signed figures. Corrected in pack version 2.

findings.title: Two approvals for the head of data
findings.text: Anita approves the pack and then the plan drawn from it, where the agreed flow has one approval.

findings.title: Send-back loop not exercised
findings.text: The first run matched the report (4.1667 / 2.7072 / 1.4595 against 4.17 / 2.71 / 1.46), so 'Send back to the architect' was never offered. Pack version 2 came from Leo's own correction, and the builder reran by itself.

findings.title: Nothing sent at go-live
findings.text: Delivery's outbox stays empty after Go live (the first email waits for the schedule), so no sent message could be shown.

findings.title: Truncated names
findings.text: Gold tables are named 'gold_monthly_performance_against_be_...' and a source 'global_equity_and_bond_i' on Pipelines.
